lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Maren Teller. I bail for the Quarter — debts, favours, the occasional drowned man. You're new. Or you're old and lost your face in the water. Which is it?

responses.text: I'm the Watch. There's been a death and I'm here to investigate it.
I don't know. I woke up next to him with no memory and a badge I don't remember earning.

memory.summary: told her the truth about the amnesia

responses.text: [Authority] I ask the questions here. Who is the dead man?

modifiers.label: She's seen harder men than you

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Watch. Right. The Watch hasn't crossed the tideline into the Quarter in three years — we're not worth the boot leather. But you're here, so. Congratulations on your assignment, detective.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: She doesn't believe you. Worse — she's decided not to mind. You've become, in one sentence, another official lie she has to manage. That costs you something you'll want back later.

responses.text: Who is he?
...That's not true. I don't actually remember who I am. I'm sorry.

memory.summary: lied about being the Watch, then admitted it

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Huh. That's the first honest thing anyone's said to me on this quay in a year. The water takes memories sometimes — we say the Drowned God keeps them. Don't laugh; people here believe it, and what people believe is half your case.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: His name was Tomas Kessler. Clerk. Kept the Mutual's books — kept MY books. Good man, bad at money, which down here is the same as saying he was drowning long before the harbour finished the job.

responses.text: Bad at money how?
What happened last night?
He has a wife?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Tomas Kessler. Our clerk. He kept the ledger that keeps this Quarter from eating itself. Now he's keeping the rain company.

responses.text: Did he have enemies? Money trouble?
Where were you last night?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Tomas owed the Mutual more than the Mutual owns. Don't look like that — it happens. You bail a man, he bails another, and one bad season the whole web of it comes due at once. He couldn't pay. Couldn't even face Edda — his wife — about it.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: A debt the Quarter could never collect. That cuts two ways: a man might end himself over it — or someone might end the debt by ending the man. File it. Both doors are open.

responses.text: I should speak to his wife.
Walk me through last night.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Third bell, I hear shouting off toward the Spindles — the Guild runs barges at night, there's always shouting. By dawn there's you, and there's Tomas, and the tide's gone out and left you both like driftwood.

responses.text: The Guild. Tell me about the barges.
That's enough for now. Thank you, Maren.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Third bell. The same hour the Guild moved cargo and the same hour, near enough, a man's lungs filled with brine. Two clocks striking together are rarely a coincidence.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Anker Voss runs the night yard. He's not a bad man, just an old one — loyal to the Guild like it's still 1955 and the whistles still blow. If Tomas saw something off those barges he shouldn't have, Voss is where you start. Mind yourself; he's built like the cranes.

responses.text: I'll pay him a visit.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Edda's in the Hall, by the stove. She's been sitting vigil since before they found him — like she knew. Be gentle. Whatever she did or didn't do, she's lost her whole world tonight.

responses.text: I'll be gentle.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: ...Tomas Kessler. Our clerk. Alright. You've got the voice for it, I'll give you that.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Good. They obey the spine, not the smile. But notice — she gave you a name and took back her warmth. You can rule this woman or befriend her. Not both.

responses.text: Money trouble? Enemies?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Or what? You'll catch cold at me?

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: She looked at the shake in your hands and weighed exactly how much of your authority is borrowed. Verdict: all of it. Try a different door.

responses.text: Fair. The truth, then — I don't remember who I am.
Just tell me who he was.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Back again. Should I expect the truth this time, or shall we keep pretending you're whatever you said you were?

responses.text: I should have been straight with you. I'm sorry.
Just answer my questions.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The honest amnesiac returns. Sit. What do you need?

responses.text: Tell me more about Tomas's debt.
The Guild barges — who runs them?
Just checking in. Thank you.
